notes: Only the first balloon circuit is built; the optional second-balloon transistor (GPIO3) extension is not included.

Breadboard rows in the images (1-30, columns a-e) map to catalogue names like '12t.c'. The left power rails are assumed to be tp (+, red) and tn (-, black); exact rail hole numbers are approximate since each rail is one strip.

The 12 ohm balloon resistor is not drawn in the images. It is modelled as twisted onto two cores of 2 m speaker cable, whose far ends are placed at 6t.d (9V rail strip, row 6 fed by the red wire) and 11t.d (transistor collector strip), as the text describes. The balloon, tape and string are not modelled.
The BC635 is a new part type with ports E, C, B (left to right with flat side towards you). Its flat side faces the ground rail; E at row 10, C at row 11, B at row 12.
The 330 ohm resistor runs from the base strip (row 12) to the GPIO2 wire strip (row 16).
Button legs are assumed on the left side (column e) of rows 1 and 3, as in the image; 1.l and 2.l are used.

Jumper wires to the Pi are pin-to-socket (jumper-wire-mf, end a on the Pi header); breadboard-only wires are pin-to-pin. Pi GND wire uses GND.1 (physical pin 6); GPIO14 is physical pin 8; GPIO2 is physical pin 3.
The 9V battery's snap leads (red/black) plug directly into the bottom + and - ends of the left rails.
